A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 28 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including equations, figures, pseudocode, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-target and real-data experiments on inversion stability, approximation quality, sampling accuracy, and runtime, with further analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Figures 1–8, Section 5, and the relocated experimental Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, augmented-state refreshment and accept/reject inversion, and the four flow constructions are retained. The broader state-space formulation changes mathematical assumptions and density reasoning without introducing a different computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Banana, Funnel, Cross, and Warped Gaussian targets, plus TReg, Brownian, SparseReg, and LGCP. The discrete and hybrid models newly mentioned in Appendix C of v2 are illustrative examples, not added experiments.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain RealNVP, NSF, NUTS, mean-field VI, and the corrected/uncorrected HMC and IRF/MCMC variants. Newly added kernel citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Training budgets, tuning grids, flow lengths, evaluation sample counts, metrics, and AIS reference procedures are unchanged. Section 5 of v2 adds the standard importance-sampling formula for the already-used normalization estimator.

E4.justification: Both retain inversion-error tests, corrected versus uncorrected stability comparisons, relative-flow and autocorrelation analyses, and ensemble-size/flow-length sensitivity experiments. Appendix C.1 of v1 matches Appendix E.1 of v2.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts and uncertainty practices match: 32-run IRF summaries, 10-run normalizing-flow summaries, standard-deviation bands, five-run tuning comparisons, and ten-run AIS reference estimates remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–8 contain identical underlying graphics content, including nested plotting objects. The numerical findings, rankings, inversion-stability thresholds, and result entries in the accompanying text are also retained.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the continuous/Lebesgue setting with a general sigma-finite base measure and relaxes Assumption 2.2 from diffeomorphic to bijective IRFs. It introduces a Radon–Nikodym formulation of the MH factor and adds Proposition C.1, its proof, and Corollary C.2. Earlier Lemma B.1 is retained as Proposition C.3.

C1.justification: The abstract and second numbered contribution now explicitly claim flows on arbitrary/general state spaces, substantially broadening v1's continuous-space setting. The three-family contribution, asymptotic-exactness claims, and empirical performance claims otherwise remain stable.

C2.justification: New Appendix C discusses applicability to discrete and hybrid spaces. v2 also removes v1's explicit qualification that the homogeneous-flow theorem requires additional differentiability, although Theorem 4.1 still assumes a diffeomorphism. Existing instability explanations and flow-choice tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix C and v2 Appendix E provide the same architectures, hyperparameters, computing platforms, AIS implementation details, and code-access information. Relocated pseudocode does not add implementation details.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tierney's general-state-space MH treatment and citations supporting kernel backgrounds and discrete/hybrid model examples. The central positioning relative to MixFlows and involutive MCMC remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main construction and flow-family sections exchange order, placing the concrete IRF construction first. All three algorithms move into appendices, and the appendix structure is reorganized around the new measure-theoretic treatment. Background and methodological passages are also rewritten.

P2.justification: The eight figures retain their panels, axes, legends, and plotted content. Figure 1 and the algorithm displays are relocated, with corresponding layout changes. Figure 7's duplicated panel label is corrected to the sequence (a)–(d).

improvement.justification: Relaxing Assumption 2.2 better accommodates the piecewise accept/reject maps, while Appendix C and the construction-first organization clarify the density argument and methodology. These gains are limited by a chain-rule denominator typo in Proposition C.1's new proof and removal of a still-relevant differentiability qualification for Theorem 4.1. The algorithms and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
